title: Apply for a licence to transport explosives or security sensitive dangerous substances
summary: This page provides information on how to apply for a licence required to transport explosives or security sensitive dangerous substances (SSDS) in NSW.
intro:
If you want to transport explosives or security sensitive dangerous substances (SSDS), you need a licence issued by SafeWork NSW.

The licence allows you to possess, transport and store the materials specified on the licence.

The licence can be issued to you or to a nominated person on behalf of a company.
who_can_apply: Hold a current NSW security clearance and ensure only people with a security clearance have unsupervised access to explosives and SSDS.
Have a legitimate reason for transporting SSDS.
Make adequate arrangements for the safe and secure handling and storage of explosives and/or SSDS.
what_you_need: Your reason(s) for requesting a licence.

A statement outlining your experience and knowledge in: training and qualifications, details of interstate explosives licence/s, details of explosives and/or SSDS to be transported, and details of explosives and/or SSDS to be stored (if applicable).
Confirmation that the quantities in the application align with the security plan and emergency plan.
Emergency contact's details, and an emergency plan.
Evidence for the submission of the emergency plan to Fire and Rescue NSW.
Evidence for the submission of the emergency plan to NSW Rural Fire Service (if the facility is located in a rural fire district).
Additional information from SafeWork NSW about transporting explosives.

how_to_steps.text: Collect all the required documentation including the material and payment needed for your SC application (if applicable).
Complete the form and submit your application with payment.

more_info.text: The nominated person for a company must be involved in the management of the company. If that person ceases to be the nominated person (for example, if they resign) the company must nominate another person to take responsibility for the licence within 7 days.
If you're lodging your application for an SC licence at the same time, it will have to be approved before your transport licence application will be processed.
The SC licence was previously called an unsupervised handling licence (UHL).
If you're storing hazardous chemicals you must notify SafeWork NSW.

faqs.q: Who needs a licence to transport explosives or SSDS?
faqs.a: If you plan to transport explosives or security sensitive dangerous substances (SSDS), you need a licence issued by SafeWork NSW.

faqs.q: Can the licence be issued to a company?
faqs.a: The licence can be issued to you or to a nominated person on behalf of a company.

faqs.q: What are the basic requirements for applying?
faqs.a: Applicants must be aged 18 or over, hold a current NSW security clearance, and have a legitimate reason for transporting SSDS.
